Then D^x is not antisymmetric (D^x_{2,1}=-1/(2Δx) but D^x_{1,2}=0) and D^{xx} is not symmetric, so the summation-by-parts identities and the D^+ identity of Lemma 1 are false as stated; moreover the matrices are not circulant, so the Fourier diagonalization D^γ E = E Λ^γ used in Lemma 3 does not hold (and D^+ is never assigned a periodic wrap entry).

issues.failure_explanation: The identity requires diag((ρ^{n+1})^2) g^{n+1}_{·β} ∈ range(X̂̂^{n+1}) for every column. But g^{n+1} = X̂̂ Ŝ̂ V̂̂^T has columns that are generic elements of range(X̂̂) = span(X̂) + span(diag(ρ^2)X̂). Applying diag(ρ^2) yields span(diag(ρ^2)X̂) + span(diag(ρ^4)X̂), and the second summand is not contained in range(X̂̂) unless ρ^{n+1} is constant. The augmentation only guarantees invariance of the components in span(X̂), not of the full S-step output of rank 4r. The same failure occurs for the V-side identity with diag(ω e^{v^2/2}). Hence P^X diag(ρ^2) g^{n+1} ≠ diag(ρ^2) g^{n+1} in general, and the subsequent reduction to the full-scheme energy identity is unjustified.
